finding: Fresh evidence shows the US duration shock broadening into synchronized sovereign/fiscal stress: US 10Y reached 5.34% (highest since 2002), France 10Y rose to 4.96% after its worst quarter since 1987 with sovereign CDS at its highest since 2013, UK 30Y exceeded 6% for the first time since 1998, and Japan sovereign yields recorded a fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit gains. European STOXX 600 fell 1.2%, indicating spillover beyond rates.
affected_assumptions: US duration stress can be modeled as primarily domestic
cross-country sovereign-rate correlations remain near prior baselines
near-term Fed expectations adequately summarize financial conditions

evidence.facts: US 10Y 5.34%; France 10Y 4.96% and worst quarter since 1987; French sovereign CDS highest since 2013; UK 30Y above 6%; Japan fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit sovereign-yield gains; STOXX 600 down 1.2%.
UK 30Y gilt 6.029%, highest since January 1998; UK 10Y 5.510%, highest since July 2007.

conflicts: Softer US PCE and reduced immediate Fed-hike expectations have not reversed long-end yield stress.
Energy prices show mixed marginal signals while sovereign yields continue rising.
AI-linked equity fundamentals remain supportive in places while sovereign discount rates rise sharply.
data_gaps: No verified order-book depth, positioning, funding, liquidation, or dealer-balance-sheet data.
Causal decomposition among fiscal risk, term premium, inflation, supply, growth and forced-position unwinds remains unresolved.
confidence: HIGH on synchronized sovereign-duration stress; MEDIUM on persistence and causal decomposition.
next_decisive_check: Test whether US 10Y remains above ~5.3%, France 10Y approaches/holds 5%, UK 30Y remains above 6%, and equity/credit spillover broadens after US payrolls; quantify cross-country rate-correlation and NQ-duration beta breaks.

oracle.finding: Promote synchronized global-duration/fiscal stress to an active ICARUS regime hypothesis; the US long-end shock is now visibly propagating through France, the UK and Japan and into European equities.

supermesh_x.finding: Reuters cross-market evidence coherently confirms rates contagion across US, French, UK and Japanese sovereign markets without requiring unavailable microstructure fields; preserve separate fiscal, inflation and energy channels rather than collapsing them into one cause.
